principles: temporary containment never claims to be a permanent fix
actively exploited systems require compromise assessment after patching
network-changing actions require explicit operator apply flag

items.action: Install all currently applicable Microsoft security updates for the deployed Windows release; reboot if required; then re-scan. This group includes the September exploited privilege-escalation issues plus earlier 2026 actively exploited Netlogon/IKE issues. Do not treat successful installation as proof that prior exploitation did not occur.
items.verify: No applicable security updates remain and installed OS build is at or above Microsoft fixed build for the deployed release.

items.action: Upgrade to a fixed RouterOS release; remove SSH/management from untrusted networks; inspect Flagged state, users, scripts and configuration after upgrade.
items.verify: Installed RouterOS is on a fixed branch release and no untrusted management exposure remains.

items.action: Install the latest applicable Jumbo Hotfix/Live Patch and prioritize Internet-facing VPN systems. Restrict management access while patching.
items.verify: Vendor patch state confirms protection for both CVEs and management exposure is restricted.

items.action: Apply SAP Security Notes 3747649 and 3759472 as applicable. Keep Message Server and administrative interfaces off untrusted networks.
items.verify: Affected kernel/message-server components report patched versions and no untrusted exposure exists.

items.action: Update Adobe Commerce/Magento to the applicable September 2026 security release (APSB26-138), then apply the CVE-2026-75650 hotfix required by APSB26-146. Review application logs, privileged credentials and filesystem state for compromise when the instance was exposed while vulnerable.
items.verify: September 2026 security release is installed, the CVE-2026-75650 hotfix is confirmed present, and compromise assessment is complete for previously exposed instances.

items.action: Upgrade to a fixed NX-OS release. Live Protect shield lp00031 may be used only as temporary mitigation after deployment impact assessment.
items.verify: Cisco Software Checker reports a fixed release; temporary shield is not counted as final remediation.

items.action: Upgrade VMware Workstation/Fusion 25H2 or 26H1 to 26H1u1. There is no vendor workaround.
items.verify: Installed product version is 26H1u1 or later.

items.action: Upgrade to the fixed maintenance release for the installed PAN-OS branch; restrict management access to a dedicated trusted path.
items.verify: Installed branch is at/above the vendor fixed release and management interface is not reachable from untrusted networks.

items.action: Require vm2 >= 3.12.2 for this snapshot, reject dangerous NodeVM configurations, and do not use same-process vm2 as the sole boundary for hostile code.
items.verify: Dependency gate passes and untrusted execution is additionally isolated at process/container/VM boundary.

items.action: Upgrade to IOS XR 26.2.2 or 26.3.1 where applicable, or move to a supported train with the complete applicable SMU set. Cisco states there is no general workaround.
items.verify: Running IOS XR release/SMU inventory matches Cisco fixed-software guidance for every applicable vulnerability class.

items.action: Update Acrobat/Reader Continuous to 26.002.21901 or later; update Acrobat 2024 Classic to 24.001.30429 or later.
items.verify: Installed track reports at least the fixed Adobe release.

items.action: Detect the documented September 2026 VDA failure signatures. Do not automatically roll back Microsoft security updates. Mark unhealthy VDAs out of service and follow Citrix/Microsoft resolution guidance when published.
items.verify: No Event 20498/6005 failure signature in the evaluation window and TermService is Running.

items.action: Upgrade self-hosted N-central to 2026.3 HF4 build 2026.3.1.14 or later. Hosted N-central is vendor-patched. Treat exposed unpatched servers as compromise-assessment candidates.
items.verify: Installed self-hosted build is >= 2026.3.1.14 and post-update authentication/admin configuration and logs have been reviewed.

items.action: Upgrade self-managed Artifactory to a fixed release for its branch or, preferably, the latest supported patch. Review administrator accounts, tokens, plugins and repository configuration after exposure.
items.verify: Installed Artifactory branch is at/above the listed fixed build and privileged configuration/tokens have been reviewed.

items.action: Upgrade affected customer-managed NetScaler to 14.1-73.32+, 13.1-63.21+, 14.1-73.32 FIPS+, or 13.1-37.277+ for FIPS/NDcPP as applicable. No generic workaround is counted as remediation.
items.verify: Installed NetScaler build meets the vendor minimum for its exact edition and affected Gateway/SAML/SIP preconditions have been reassessed.

items.action: Upgrade SMA1000 to 12.4.3-03526 or 12.5.0-02952 as applicable. If compromise indicators are found, re-image/redeploy and rotate user/admin passwords and TOTP material per vendor guidance.
items.verify: Installed platform-hotfix is at/above the fixed build for the branch and vendor IoC review is complete.

items.action: Upgrade ASA/FTD to a Cisco-fixed release for the deployed train. There is no vendor workaround; do not count rate limiting or signatures as final remediation.
items.verify: Cisco Software Checker/advisory confirms the exact deployed ASA/FTD release is fixed for CVE-2026-20349.

items.action: Install all applicable SharePoint cumulative/security updates through the current supported level. This policy covers the March and July 2026 actively exploited SharePoint families. For any internet-exposed instance that was vulnerable, enable/verify AMSI Full Mode where supported, perform compromise assessment, and rotate credentials/secrets and SharePoint machine keys that could have been exposed.
items.verify: SharePoint farm build and required prerequisite updates match Microsoft guidance; PSConfig/update completion is verified and compromise assessment is closed.

items.action: Upgrade Gitea to at least 1.27.1; prefer the latest supported release. Review repository hooks, service-account activity and host processes if the instance was reachable by untrusted users.
items.verify: Gitea version is >= 1.27.1 and repository hook/configuration review shows no unauthorized persistence.

items.action: Upgrade MLflow to >= 3.15.0 and keep the tracking server behind authentication/network controls. Block workload access to cloud metadata endpoints where not explicitly required.
items.verify: MLflow is >= 3.15.0 and webhook/egress controls prevent access to loopback, internal-only and cloud-metadata targets.

items.action: Apply SAP Security Note 3798315 and update the affected sap/cds-mtxs line to the fixed release specified by SAP for the deployed branch.
items.verify: Dependency/version inventory is outside the affected ranges and SAP Security Note 3798315 remediation is recorded.

items.action: Apply SAP Security Note 3781729 to affected SAP GUI for Java 8.10 deployments.
items.verify: SAP GUI for Java deployment is patched according to Security Note 3781729.

items.action: Update Chrome to at least 153.0.8010.36 on Linux and at least 153.0.8010.37 on Windows/macOS for this snapshot, then restart the browser so the updated binary is active. Managed fleets should enforce the update rather than relying on user restart.
items.verify: Running Chrome version meets the fixed build for the asset platform and managed update status reports no pending restart/update.

items.action: Upgrade GitLab immediately to 19.1.8, 19.2.6, 19.3.2 or a later supported fixed release. Review privileged users, tokens, hooks, runners and recent administrative changes when an affected instance was reachable by untrusted users.
items.verify: Installed GitLab branch is at or above its fixed patch release and compromise review is complete for exposed affected instances.

items.action: Update supported macOS systems to the branch release that contains the Screen Sharing authentication fix. Disable or firewall Screen Sharing from untrusted networks when it is not explicitly required; investigate exposed vulnerable hosts for unauthorized access.
items.verify: Running macOS is at/above the fixed branch release and Screen Sharing exposure is explicitly authorized and constrained.

products: SAP Commerce Cloud Data Hub Adapter
items.action: Apply SAP Security Note 3771065 and move SAP Commerce Cloud 2211/JDK21 to a current supported update release. For previously exposed vulnerable deployments, review application/admin activity and integration credentials for compromise.
items.verify: SAP Security Note 3771065 remediation is recorded and the deployment uses a current supported Commerce Cloud update release.

items.action: Use the current Fortinet PSIRT advisory/upgrade-path tool for the deployed FortiOS train and move to a fixed supported release. Because CISA added CVE-2025-25249 to KEV in September 2026, exposed previously affected appliances require compromise assessment in addition to patching.
items.verify: Fortinet PSIRT/upgrade-path guidance confirms the exact deployed release is not affected and compromise assessment is closed for previously exposed vulnerable systems.

items.action: Apply the current Ivanti EPMM vendor hotfix/fixed supported release for CVE-2026-1281 and CVE-2026-1340. Preserve forensic evidence before remediation on exposed appliances and re-apply any vendor RPM hotfix after an upgrade if Ivanti guidance for the deployed train requires it.
items.verify: Ivanti guidance confirms the exact deployed EPMM release/hotfix state is fixed and forensic review is closed for previously exposed vulnerable appliances.

items.action: Upgrade the deployed Catalyst SD-WAN Controller/Manager train to a Cisco-fixed supported release. Preserve evidence, review configuration and authentication/peering logs for unauthorized access, and remove direct Internet exposure from management/control-plane interfaces.
items.verify: Cisco advisory/Software Checker confirms the exact deployed train is fixed and the compromise hunt/configuration review is closed.

items.action: Update affected NetScaler ADC/Gateway to a currently supported fixed release. The March fixes began at 14.1-66.59, 13.1-62.23 and 13.1-37.262 FIPS/NDcPP; later August 2026 security builds supersede these. Restrict exposed Gateway/AAA access until updated and invalidate active/persistent sessions after patching.
items.verify: Current Citrix guidance confirms the exact edition/build is fixed for both the March and later 2026 NetScaler advisories, and sessions were invalidated where required.

items.action: Install the distribution kernel that fixes CVE-2026-31431. Until the vendor-fixed kernel is active, disable algif_aead persistently and unload it when operationally safe; block AF_ALG in container/CI seccomp profiles where untrusted workloads execute. Use scripts/linux/mitigate-copy-fail.sh for an explicit-gate local mitigation.
items.verify: Distribution security tracker reports the running kernel fixed, or the interim algif_aead/AF_ALG mitigation is verified until reboot into a fixed kernel.

items.action: Upgrade to a Palo Alto fixed release for the exact PAN-OS train. Until fixed, disable User-ID Authentication Portal if not required or restrict it to trusted zones only. Previously Internet-exposed affected firewalls require compromise assessment because Palo Alto observed exploitation.
items.verify: Vendor advisory confirms the exact PAN-OS build is fixed for CVE-2026-0300 and User-ID Authentication Portal exposure is authorized/constrained.

items.action: Update Ivanti Sentry using the current vendor-fixed release/hotfix for the deployed branch. Prioritize Internet-facing appliances and restrict management/service exposure to trusted networks until remediation is verified.
items.verify: Ivanti guidance confirms the exact deployed Sentry version is fixed for CVE-2026-10520 and CVE-2026-10523.

items.action: Upgrade ScreenConnect to 26.6.5 or later. Cloud deployments are vendor-updated; on-premises deployments must upgrade and update/reinstall host/access clients as directed by ConnectWise. If immediate upgrade is impossible, temporarily remove TransferFiles/TransferFilesInSession permission from roles. Because CISA lists this CVE as actively exploited and requiring forensic triage, review users, roles, audit logs and connected systems after remediation.
items.verify: ScreenConnect reports version >= 26.6.5, relevant clients/agents are updated, temporary file-transfer restrictions are either retained or deliberately restored after patch validation, and compromise triage is closed for exposed systems.

scope: Bounded high-signal snapshot of officially disclosed issues verified through 2026-09-14 that are actively exploited, critical with a published remediation, or operationally critical to safe patching. It is not a claim to enumerate every vulnerability worldwide.
source_scope: Vendor security advisories and release notes
CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities evidence where directly or government-source corroborated
Canadian Centre for Cyber Security alerts/advisories
GitHub Security Advisories for covered open-source projects
